scroll.title: Bolo Knife
scroll.description: Standard-issue weapon of Filipino guerrilla fighters during the Battle of Bataan, 1942.
scroll.location: GPS Test Location 1

scroll.title: M2 60mm Mortar
scroll.description: The M2 60mm Mortar was a light infantry mortar used by American and Filipino forces during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: GPS Test Location 2

scroll.title: Thompson Submachine Gun
scroll.description: The Thompson Submachine Gun, known as the Tommy Gun, was widely used by American forces during World War II.
scroll.location: GPS Test Location 3

scroll.title: M1 Steel Helmet
scroll.description: The M1 steel helmet was standard headgear for American and Filipino USAFFE soldiers throughout the Battle of Bataan (January-April 1942).
scroll.location: Weapons & Equipment Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1911A1 Automatic Pistol
scroll.description: The Colt M1911A1 .45 caliber automatic pistol was the standard sidearm of American officers and senior non-commissioned officers defending Bataan.
scroll.location: Officers' Armory Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1918A2 Browning Automatic Rifle
scroll.description: The Browning Automatic Rifle M1918A2 was the backbone of automatic firepower for USAFFE rifle squads during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Heavy Weapons Gallery — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1903 Springfield Bolt-Action Rifle
scroll.description: The M1903 Springfield was the primary service rifle of both Filipino and American USAFFE infantry at the outbreak of WWII.
scroll.location: Weapons Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1917 Enfield Rifle
scroll.description: A WWI-era bolt-action rifle reissued to Philippine Army troops in 1941 to supplement limited M1903 Springfield supplies.
scroll.location: Weapons Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1911A1 Colt .45 Pistol
scroll.description: The M1911A1 semi-automatic pistol was the standard sidearm issued to USAFFE officers, NCOs, and crew-served weapon teams during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Officers' Armory Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1905/M1 Bayonet
scroll.description: The M1905 bayonet, designed for mounting on the M1903 Springfield rifle, featured a 40.6 cm blade for close-quarters combat.
scroll.location: Weapons Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Mk 2 "Pineapple" Fragmentation Grenade
scroll.description: The Mk 2 fragmentation grenade, nicknamed the "Pineapple" for its segmented cast-iron body, was standard issue for USAFFE infantry at Bataan.
scroll.location: Ordnance Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1923 Cartridge Belt
scroll.description: The M1923 Dismounted Cartridge Belt held ten five-round clips of .30-06 Springfield ammunition, giving each rifleman immediate access to 50 rounds.
scroll.location: Equipment Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1919A4 Browning .30 Cal Machine Gun
scroll.description: The M1919A4 Browning .30 caliber air-cooled machine gun was the primary medium support weapon of USAFFE infantry during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Heavy Weapons Gallery — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1910 Canteen with Cup & Cover
scroll.description: The M1910 canteen and its aluminum cup were indispensable survival items for every USAFFE soldier at Bataan.
scroll.location: Field Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Bamboo Stretcher
scroll.description: The bamboo stretcher was a vital piece of improvised medical equipment used by Filipino medics and soldiers during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Medical Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Type 38 Arisaka Rifle
scroll.description: The Type 38 Arisaka was the primary bolt-action infantry rifle of the Imperial Japanese Army during the assault on the Philippines and the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Enemy Forces Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Type 96 Light Machine Gun
scroll.description: The Type 96 Light Machine Gun was the standard squad automatic weapon of Japanese infantry during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Enemy Forces Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Type 89 Grenade Discharger
scroll.description: The Type 89 Grenade Discharger, misnamed the "knee mortar" by Allied soldiers, was an extremely versatile and feared weapon of Japanese infantry squads at Bataan.
scroll.location: Enemy Forces Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Japanese Rice Ration Sack
scroll.description: The rice ration sack was a fundamental part of the Imperial Japanese soldier's field kit during the Bataan campaign.
scroll.location: Japanese Forces Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Japanese Propaganda Leaflet
scroll.description: Imperial Japanese forces dropped propaganda leaflets over Bataan by aircraft and fired them in artillery shells as a psychological warfare tool.
scroll.location: Historical Documents — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1 81mm Mortar
scroll.description: The M1 81mm Mortar provided USAFFE forces at Bataan with crucial medium indirect-fire support at the battalion level.
scroll.location: Artillery Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: HBT Herringbone Twill Fatigue Uniform
scroll.description: The Herringbone Twill (HBT) two-piece fatigue uniform was the working and combat dress of American soldiers in the Pacific Theater during WWII.
scroll.location: Uniforms & Equipment Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1938 Canvas Leggings
scroll.description: The M1938 Canvas Leggings were worn over the lower leg and boot by American soldiers at Bataan.
scroll.location: Uniforms & Equipment Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Army Service Shoe (Leather)
scroll.description: The standard-issue Army leather service shoe proved problematic in Bataan's jungle terrain, where mud, water crossings, and sharp terrain quickly deteriorated the leather.
scroll.location: Uniforms & Equipment Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M2A2 Service Gas Mask
scroll.description: The M2A2 Lightweight Service Gas Mask was issued to USAFFE soldiers as protection against potential Japanese chemical weapons use.
scroll.location: Protective Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1936 Web Pistol Belt
scroll.description: The M1936 Web Pistol Belt was the primary load-bearing belt for USAFFE officers and pistol-armed soldiers at Bataan.
scroll.location: Equipment Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1936 Field Suspenders
scroll.description: The M1936 Field Suspenders were paired with the M1936 Pistol Belt and M1923 Cartridge Belt to distribute the weight of a soldier's combat load during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Equipment Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

specs.value: M1936 Pistol Belt, M1923 Cartridge Belt

scroll.title: M1928 Haversack
scroll.description: The M1928 Haversack was the standard individual field pack of American infantrymen at Bataan.
scroll.location: Field Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1938 Canvas Map Case
scroll.description: The M1938 Canvas Map Case was carried by USAFFE officers during the Battle of Bataan to protect maps, operational orders, and intelligence reports from tropical humidity and rain.
scroll.location: Officers' Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1907 Rifle Sling
scroll.description: The M1907 leather rifle sling was standard issue for the M1903 Springfield and M1 Garand rifles carried by every USAFFE infantryman at Bataan.
scroll.location: Field Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1910 T-Handle Entrenching Tool
scroll.description: The M1910 T-Handle Entrenching Tool was carried by every USAFFE infantryman defending Bataan.
scroll.location: Field Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1938 Lensatic Compass
scroll.description: The M1938 Lensatic Compass was the standard military compass issued to American officers and NCOs during the Bataan campaign.
scroll.location: Officers' Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: EE-8 Field Telephone
scroll.description: The EE-8 Field Telephone was the primary tactical communications device used by USAFFE units during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Communications Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Atabrine (Quinacrine) Medicine
scroll.description: Atabrine — quinacrine hydrochloride — was the synthetic anti-malarial drug administered to American and Filipino USAFFE soldiers at Bataan.
scroll.location: Medical Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: M1942 First Aid Pouch
scroll.description: The M1942 First Aid Pouch was standard-issue medical equipment carried by every USAFFE infantryman at Bataan.
scroll.location: Medical Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

specs.value: Field dressing, iodine, sulfanilamide, morphine syrette

scroll.title: M3 Binoculars
scroll.description: Military binoculars were essential observation tools for USAFFE officers and scouts during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Officers' Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Carlisle Model First Aid Bandage
scroll.description: The Carlisle Model First Aid Bandage was the standard individual field dressing issued to every USAFFE soldier at Bataan.
scroll.location: Medical Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Identification Tags (Dog Tags)
scroll.description: Military identification tags — called dog tags — were worn by every USAFFE soldier at Bataan bearing name, serial number, blood type, and religion.
scroll.location: Personal Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: TL-122 Military Flashlight
scroll.description: The TL-122 angle-head flashlight was standard issue for American soldiers in the Pacific Theater.
scroll.location: Field Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Morphine Tartrate Syrette
scroll.description: The morphine syrette — a collapsible metal tube with an attached needle — delivered a 30mg dose of morphine tartrate for battlefield pain management.
scroll.location: Medical Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Nambu Type 14 Pistol
scroll.description: The Nambu Type 14 semi-automatic pistol was the standard sidearm of Imperial Japanese Army officers during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Enemy Forces Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Senninbari — Thousand Stitches Belt
scroll.description: A white cotton "thousand-stitch" belt, each stitch sewn by a different woman as a charm for protection and good fortune.
scroll.location: Japanese Cultural Artifacts — Mt. Samat Shrine

specs.value: White cotton with red silk stitches

scroll.title: M1934 Shelter Half
scroll.description: The M1934 Shelter Half was the individual field shelter carried by every USAFFE infantryman at Bataan.
scroll.location: Field Equipment Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Type 90 Steel Combat Helmet
scroll.description: The Type 90 Steel Combat Helmet was the standard headgear of Imperial Japanese Army soldiers who assaulted the Bataan Peninsula in 1942.
scroll.location: Enemy Forces Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Type 92 Heavy Machine Gun
scroll.description: Nicknamed the "woodpecker" for its slow firing rhythm, it was the Imperial Japanese Army's primary heavy machine gun at Bataan.
scroll.location: Enemy Forces Display — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Bolo Knife
scroll.description: Standard-issue weapon of Filipino guerrilla fighters during the Battle of Bataan, 1942.
scroll.location: Weapons Display, West Wing — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Type 38 Arisaka Rifle
scroll.description: Primary bolt-action rifle of the Imperial Japanese Army during the Battle of Bataan, 1942.
scroll.location: North Entrance — Memorial Grounds

scroll.title: 21st Division - Mountain Watchers
scroll.description: The 21st Division was one of the ten reserve divisions of the Philippine Army mobilized in 1941.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Dambana ng Kagitingan
scroll.description: The Shrine of Valor stands atop Mt. Samat in Bataan, Philippines.
scroll.location: Summit — Mt. Samat National Shrine

scroll.title: USAFFE
scroll.description: The USAFFE eagle emblem represents the combined American-Filipino command that fought the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 11th Division
scroll.description: The 11th Division was one of the Philippine Army reserve divisions mobilized in 1941 and deployed to defend the Bataan Peninsula.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 41st Division
scroll.description: The 41st Division, Philippine Army was mobilized in 1941 and fought under I Corps during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 51st Division
scroll.description: The 51st Division, Philippine Army served under II Corps during the Battle of Bataan, defending the eastern sector of the Bataan defensive lines.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 71st Division
scroll.description: The 71st Division, Philippine Army was a reserve division mobilized in 1941 and assigned to I Corps during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 91st Division
scroll.description: The 91st Division, Philippine Army was mobilized from the Visayas region and deployed to Bataan as part of the USAFFE defense.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Air Corps
scroll.description: The Philippine Army Air Corps was the air arm of the Philippine Army at the outbreak of WWII.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: PN Off Shore Patrol
scroll.description: The Philippine Navy Off Shore Patrol was the naval component of USAFFE during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 1st Regular Division
scroll.description: The 1st Regular Division was the premier regular combat division of the Philippine Army — composed of professional soldiers rather than reservists.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 2nd Regular Division
scroll.description: The 2nd Regular Division was the second of the Philippine Army's professional regular divisions deployed at Bataan.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 31st Division
scroll.description: The 31st Division, Philippine Army was a reserve division mobilized in 1941 and assigned to I Corps during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 81st Division
scroll.description: The 81st Division, Philippine Army was a reserve division mobilized from the Visayas in 1941 and deployed to Bataan under I Corps.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 101st Division
scroll.description: The 101st Division, Philippine Army was one of the last reserve divisions committed to the Bataan defense.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: 61st Division
scroll.description: The 61st Division was one of the Philippine Army's reserve divisions mobilized in 1941 as part of the Bataan defense order of battle.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: HPA
scroll.description: HPA, Headquarters Philippine Army, was the central command overseeing all Philippine Army divisions during the Battle of Bataan.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Philippine Department
scroll.description: The Philippine Department was the U.S. Army's administrative command in the Philippines before USAFFE was formed in July 1941.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine

scroll.title: Philippine Division
scroll.description: The Philippine Division was a U.S. Army division that included the 31st U.S. Infantry and Philippine Scout regiments, among the most distinguished formations in the Pacific.
scroll.location: Division Emblems Hall — Mt. Samat Shrine
